text:
marco: Heads-up — we saw a 99th-percentile latency spike for hosted-small around 09:12 UTC and a correlated throughput drop. Scale-controller wakeups were delayed ~6-9s. Noticed more kernel_fallback hits in runtime logs.

devon: Looking at prometheus: scale_controller.queue_length spiked, warm-pool stayed at min size. Could be autoscaler backoff or warm-pool prefetch failing. Any kernel-selection logs?

sre-bot: ALERT: latency_surge detected for service=hosted-small (09:12 UTC). Incident created: INC-412.

anya: Posting quick profiler excerpt and kernel selector snippet below — looks like many requests ended up on unoptimized kernel paths.

anya: ```
[09:12:18] kernel_selector: model=model-x seq_len=512 chosen_kernel=generic_attention_v1 fallback=true
[09:12:18] batcher: batch_size=4 latency_ms=87 kv_cache_hit=false
[09:12:19] perf: cpu_ms=45 gpu_ms=120 kv_prefetch_ms=30
```

lee: KV cache hitrate dropped from ~94% -> 62% at the same time window. That explains extra work per request and more cache prefetch pressure. Node gpu-m0 reported a memory spike and eviction noise. Might be noisy neighbor.

sara: Did we deploy any batching or kernel selector changes yesterday? I remember a batching-hysteresis tweak went out in the afternoon.

devon: We rolled batching-hysteresis to canary at 08:40 but not full. Kernel selector tweak landed in the runtime yesterday evening (PR #1987) — it added a new heuristic for seq_len routing.

marco: Traces show a pattern: requests that missed KV cache often had seq_len ~400-700 and hit the fallback kernel path which is much slower. Combined with autoscaler wakeup backoff, new capacity wasn't provisioned quickly.

anya: Another snippet from runtime logs:
```
[09:12:20] kv_cache: miss key_prefix=... prefetch_start
[09:12:20] warm_pool: prefetch_task queued for node=gpu-m0
[09:12:21] kernel_selector: no optimized kernel for seq_len=512 on model-x -> fallback
[09:12:22] container: prefetcher OOM, killed pid=4321
```

lee: That prefetcher OOM is key — if prefetcher gets killed, warmpool entries get evicted and hitrate plummets. Node-level noisy neighbor (batch job) caused memory churn.

devon: The autoscaler backoff logic has a subtle bug: when warm-pool size is changed rapidly, the controller's backoff timer doesn't reset, so wakeups are postponed. I can reproduce locally.

sara: I found the buggy condition: backoff reset checked pool_delta == 0 instead of pool_delta != 0 in v2 of the controller. Opening hotfix PR now.

marco: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily increase warm-pool.min by +2 in affected region, 2) disable kernel_fallback for seq_len>256 (force optimized path or explicit error), 3) roll back the new kernel-selector heuristic if needed. Which order?

devon: Do 1 and 2 asap. Disabling fallback reduces perf variability even if it increases rejections slightly. I'll prepare a small change to flags.

marco: I'll scale warm-pool by +2 for us-west-2 and eu-west-1 now.

sre-bot: ACTION: warm-pool min increased for hosted-small us-west-2 at 09:24 UTC.

devon: Pushed flag to runtime to disable fallback for seq_len>256 on canary at 09:27. Monitoring.

sre-bot: UPDATE: mitigation applied. Latency trending down 09:37 UTC. Keep an eye on kernel_fallback_rate and kv_cache_hitrate.

anya: Preliminary root-cause summary for the postmortem: combination of (A) KV cache eviction due to prefetcher OOM on a noisy node, (B) increased kernel_fallback rate for mid-to-high seq_len after recent selector heuristic change, and (C) autoscaler wakeup backoff bug that delayed provisioning. All three amplified each other.

devon: Follow-ups (owners):
- devon: add kernel_fallback_rate metric + alert, gather perf traces for model-x across seq_len buckets
- sara: land autoscaler hotfix + unit test for backoff reset, schedule canary rollout
- lee: investigate prefetcher memory usage, add OOM alerts and pod qos adjustments
- anya: write full incident postmortem with flamegraphs and traces

marco: Assigning owners: devon -> kernel metrics & traces, sara -> autoscaler fix, lee -> warmpool prefetch stability, anya -> postmortem writeup. I'll follow up on rollback plan if trends don't improve.

sara: :thumbsup: PR opened for autoscaler fix and test coverage (PR #2045).

devon: I'll collect perf traces into the incident ticket and add dashboards for kernel_fallback_rate by model+seq_len.

marco: Timeline note: incident opened ~09:13 UTC, mitigation applied ~09:24-09:27 UTC, service metrics normalized by ~09:38 UTC. Closing monitoring window in 1h unless we see recurrence.

anya: Adding links: dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/hosted-small/latency, traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/INC-412

lee: Quick note: we should also consider making the warmpool prefetcher more memory conservative and ensure evicted entries get rehydrated asynchronously without blocking critical requests.

marco: Good plan. Thanks everyone — we'll capture action items in the postmortem and schedule follow-ups.

sre-bot: Incident INC-412 status: mitigated. Next update in postmortem.
